summary.intent: Close a race where addrConn.connect() and addrConn.updateAddrs() could each observe ac.state == Idle and start a second, parallel resetTransport, because the caller released ac.mu before resetTransport re-acquired it; the fix holds ac.mu continuously from the Idle check through the transition to Connecting.
summary.issue_fit: Met — issue #7365's own root-cause comment (arjan-bal, 2024-07-04T07:02:02Z) proposed exactly this fix ("set the state to connecting while addrConn.connect has the mutex locked"), and the diff implements it: connect() and updateAddrs() no longer unlock before calling resetTransportAndUnlock, which now sets Connecting before its first unlock.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff reviewed (clientconn.go, the only changed file). Both call sites into resetTransportAndUnlock and every one of its unlock/return paths were traced against base and head. `go build ./...` and 5x `-race` runs of the targeted regression test (Test/AuthorityRevive) passed once at the pinned head. Two concurrency safety premises about the new lock-holding/goroutine-handoff contract were sent to an independent fresh-context verifier; both were ruled `holds`. Retrospective, fully offline review of a merged PR: no gh/network access was available, so the forge packet was reconstructed from the caller-supplied frozen packet text, preserving every title, body, timestamp, author, state, and comment verbatim; only internal numeric ids and comment URLs (never given in that text) are synthesized placeholders.

observations.fact: Removing the explicit `ac.mu.Unlock()` before `go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock()` in updateAddrs (clientconn.go:996) means the same goroutine's deferred `ac.transport.GracefulClose()` (clientconn.go:986) now runs while ac.mu is still held, and GracefulClose synchronously reaches the onClose closure (clientconn.go:1351), which itself calls ac.mu.Lock(); this path now briefly blocks on the spawned goroutine's own unlock instead of running lock-free as it did before this change.

The new private contract on resetTransportAndUnlock, that ac.mu is held by the caller on entry, is enforced only by its doc comment and Go's unlock-of-an-unlocked-mutex panic, not by a code-level check; reviewers explicitly discussed and declined adding one.

Preventing the second parallel connection attempt removes the orphaned transport.

tasks.premise: Every call path reaching resetTransportAndUnlock (clientconn.go:1234) already holds ac.mu exactly once, and every return path inside it unlocks ac.mu exactly once, so the function can never leave ac.mu double-locked, double-unlocked, or leaked.
tasks.evidence: clientconn.go:905-923 (connect), :985-996 (updateAddrs), :1234-1302 (all entry/return paths); independently re-traced against updateConnectivityState at :1200-1215.

tasks.premise: Spawning `go ac.resetTransportAndUnlock()` in updateAddrs while ac.mu is still held, immediately followed by the deferred GracefulClose->onClose in the same goroutine (which re-locks ac.mu), cannot deadlock: the spawned goroutine's path to its own first ac.mu.Unlock() never depends on the updateAddrs goroutine making further progress.
